+---
+"@sitoo/iam-mono-iam-api": minor
+---
+
+Add `GET /v1/scoped-user-role-assignments`: a paginated list of the users who have
+access at a given `(environment, account_id, site_id, store_id)` scope point.
+
+An assignment is in scope when it was granted at the requested scope point or above
+it (organization → account → site → store); a grant more specific than the query
+point does not match. Per user, only the assignments at the deepest matching level
+are returned, and assignments are returned with their scope unmodified.
+
+IAM assignments only — this route has no legacy platform-framework fallback. It is
+exempt from the rolesv2 feature gate as a read-only route, so it stays reachable when
+the platform-framework flag check is unavailable. Organizations that have not adopted
+rolesv2 hold no IAM assignments, so the endpoint returns an empty list rather than
+legacy data.
+
+Adds migration `008_scoped_assignment_lookup_index`, which replaces `idx_user_org` on
+`user_role_assignments` with `idx_ura_org_env_user_scope (organization_id, environment,
+user_id, account_id, site_id, store_id)`. The new endpoint filters by organization and
+environment and sorts by user id, which the old index could not serve. Every existing read
+filters organization and environment alongside user id, so the replacement serves them
+unchanged and measurably speeds up inserts. The index is built without `CONCURRENTLY`
+because migrations run inside a transaction; it takes a `SHARE` lock, so reads continue and
+writes pause for the duration of the build.

@@ -0,0 +1,200 @@
+# Scoped user role assignments
+
+## Goal
+
+Answer the question "who has access here?" — given a scope point
+`(environment, account_id, site_id, store_id)`, return the users who can act at it,
+paginated, each with the role assignment(s) that grant it.
+
+The existing reads answer the opposite question. `GET /v1/role-assignments` and
+`GET /v1/user-role-assignments` both require `user_ids` and treat the scope ids as
+exact-match filters, so `site_id=5` never matches an account-level row (its `site_id`
+is NULL). There is no way to go from a scope to its users.
+
+New route: `GET /v1/scoped-user-role-assignments`.
+
+## Scope resolution
+
+The query point is the scope asked for. An assignment is in scope when it was granted
+**at that point or above** it — walk up only.
+
+```text
+query: account=1, site=5, store=7
+
+IN   org      (null, null, null)   level 1
+IN   account  (1,    null, null)   level 2
+IN   site     (1,    5,    null)   level 3
+IN   store    (1,    5,    7)      level 4
+OUT  anything else
+```
+
+A grant *more specific* than the query point does not match: a store-only grant confers
+no access to the whole site. Asking about a site therefore excludes users who only hold
+one of its stores.
+
+Per user, only the assignments at the deepest matching level are returned. Ties at that
+level all survive — two site-level assignments both come back.
+
+The consequence worth stating explicitly: **the winning assignment depends on the query
+point.** A user holding both a site grant and a store grant resolves to the store one
+when queried at that store, and to the site one when queried at the site. If their store
+grant is for a *different* store, they resolve to the site grant again.
+
+Levels reuse `HIERARCHY_LEVEL` (`src/types.ts`) and `getHierarchyLevel`
+(`src/utils/ranking.ts`) rather than re-deriving the ordering.
+
+## Assignments are returned unmodified
+
+An assignment covering stores 7, 8 and 9, matched by a query for store 7, is returned
+with `store_ids: [7, 8, 9]`. The endpoint *selects* assignments; it does not rewrite them
+to the part that matched.
+
+This constrains the read strategy. The obvious implementation — filter rows in SQL by the
+scope predicate — silently truncates a fan-out, because `roleAssignmentRowsToDomain`
+reassembles the id arrays from whichever rows survived. So scope matching has to happen on
+the assembled domain object, after all of an assignment's rows are in hand.
+
+## Read strategy
+
+Two queries, because pagination is over **users** rather than rows — a page must never be
+half a user.
+
+1. **Which users are on this page.** `SELECT DISTINCT user_id` with the walk-up predicate
+   in SQL, keyset on `user_id ASC`, `LIMIT num + 1` to detect `hasMore`.
+2. **Their assignments.** Every row for exactly those users, joined to `roles`, with **no**
+   scope predicate — so each assignment reassembles with its full scope.
+
+Scope matching and most-specific selection then run as pure functions over the domain
+objects. Row volume is bounded: `MAX_ASSIGNMENTS_PER_USER` is 20 and fan-out caps at 50
+ids, so step 2 reads at most `num` × a small constant.
+
+Cursor reuses `encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor` with `user_id` in the existing `id` field; no
+new cursor shape.
+
+### Accepted cost: the rule is expressed twice
+
+The SQL predicate (`buildScopePredicate`) and the JS predicate
+(`roleAssignmentMatchesScope`) encode the same rule at different layers. Pagination-by-user
+forces this: step 1 must decide page membership in the database, before any domain object
+exists.
+
+Mitigation rather than elimination — the service drops any user left with no surviving
+assignment, so a divergence degrades into a shorter page instead of a group with an empty
+`assignments` array, and an e2e test asserts that never happens.
+
+## Indexing
+
+The scope-first read is a new access pattern for this table. Every pre-existing read filters
+`user_id` first, which is why `idx_user_org (user_id, organization_id, environment)` fits them;
+the paging query instead filters `organization_id, environment` and *sorts* by `user_id`.
+
+Decision: **replace** `idx_user_org` with
+
+```sql
+idx_ura_org_env_user_scope
+  (organization_id, environment, user_id, account_id, site_id, store_id)
+```
+
+`(organization_id, environment)` serves the seek, `user_id` serves the `ORDER BY` and the cursor
+range, and the trailing scope columns make the index cover every column the scoped query touches,
+so it can be answered index-only.
+
+Measured on 1.24M rows across 60 organizations, median of repeated runs:
+
+| Index | Scoped query | Existing reads | 3000-row insert | Total index bytes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| none (status quo) | 30–72 ms | 0.17 ms | 257 ms | 130 MB |
+| add the new index (4 indexes) | 0.02–2.8 ms | 0.17 ms | 292 ms | 157 MB |
+| **replace `idx_user_org` (3 indexes)** | **0.02–2.8 ms** | **0.16 ms** | **206 ms** | 144 MB |
+
+Replacing is not merely write-neutral, it is ~20% *faster* on insert than the status quo: the new
+index leads with low-cardinality `organization_id`, so one assignment's store fan-out lands in a
+few adjacent pages, whereas `idx_user_org` led with a effectively random `user_id`. It also newly
+serves two reads `idx_user_org` could not — the seeder's `SELECT DISTINCT organization_id` and the
+effective-permissions report's org+env scan.
+
+Replacing is safe because **every** read of this table that filters `user_id` also filters
+`organization_id` and `environment` (audited across `role-assignments.db.ts`, `roles.db.ts`,
+`audit.service.ts`, and the seeder). The only reads that do not mention `user_id` go by
+`assignment_id` or `role_id` and are served by their own indexes.
+
+### Rejected alternatives
+
+- **`(organization_id, environment, user_id)`** — 45–56 ms, barely better than no index and
+  *worse* than the status quo at the account and site query points. Without the scope columns the
+  predicate cannot be evaluated from the index, so every candidate row needs a heap visit.
+- **`(organization_id, environment, user_id) INCLUDE (account_id, site_id, store_id)`** —
+  68–72 ms and 77 MB, three times the chosen index for worse performance. `INCLUDE` columns
+  cannot be used as index qualifications, so they filter nothing here; they only add bulk.
+  This shape looks attractive and is a trap.
+- **`(organization_id, environment, account_id, site_id, store_id, user_id)`** — 1.7 ms scoped,
+  but 6.4 ms on the existing hot read (38x worse) because `user_id` is no longer near the leading
+  edge, so it cannot replace `idx_user_org`.
+- **`(organization_id, environment, account_id, site_id, store_id)`** — 67 ms on the existing
+  read. Rejected outright.
+
+### Operational notes
+
+`CREATE INDEX` is deliberately **not** `CONCURRENTLY`: `migrate.ts` runs each migration inside a
+transaction (`db.transaction().execute(...)`), and `CONCURRENTLY` cannot run in a transaction
+block — verified, it raises `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block`. The
+plain build took 2.7 s for 1.24M rows and takes a `SHARE` lock, so reads continue and writes pause
+for the duration. `DROP INDEX` is ~2 ms.
+
+Plan choice is not fully stable, and both branches are acceptable. At the account and site query
+points the planner picks an index-only scan with `LIMIT` early exit (0.02 ms). At the full store
+query point, where the predicate has four `OR` branches, it switches to `BitmapOr` plus a `Sort`
+(~2.8 ms). Forcing the faster plan would mean rewriting the query as a `UNION ALL` of four ordered
+branches — not worth it for the difference.
+
+## Interface decisions
+
+**`account_id` is required.** Every service caller carries `auth.accountId` (Basic auth
+rejects a caller without one), and `assertAuthMatchesRequest` 403s a mismatch, so
+cross-account queries are impossible by construction. An org-wide query point was
+considered and rejected: under walk-up it would match only org-level grants, which
+`createAssignment` refuses to create (`single-account-only`), so it would near-always
+return `[]`.
+
+**`store_id` requires `site_id`** — 400 `invalid-scope`. Store rows always carry a site,
+so a store without a site describes no reachable row.
+
+**Response reuses `UserRoleAssignmentGroupSchema`**, the shape
+`GET /v1/user-role-assignments` already returns, in the standard `{ items, next }`
+envelope. Nothing new for clients to learn.
+
+**IAM assignments only — no legacy fallback.** `legacyForUsers` resolves *known* user ids
+against platform-framework; it cannot enumerate, so it has no meaning on a discovery
+endpoint. Organizations that have not adopted rolesv2 hold no IAM assignments and get an
+empty list.
+
+**Exempt from the rolesv2 gate.** `ROLESV2_EXEMPT_ROUTES` states its own policy as
+"read-only routes that stay reachable when rolesv2 is off" — it is not about legacy
+fallback, since `GET /roles` and `GET /role-by-slug` are exempt with none. Decisive
+factor: the middleware fails closed, treating rolesv2 as disabled on any
+platform-framework transport error, explicitly "so exempt GETs keep working". Without the
+exemption a PF blip would 403 this route even for fully migrated orgs — for a read that
+touches only the IAM database and calls PF not at all.
+
+## Testing notes
+
+`buildScopePredicate` is asserted on the actual `(column, operator, value)` triples it emits, not
+on the number of `OR` branches. Branch counting is worthless here: a predicate comparing `site_id`
+to the *account* id, one missing a `store_id IS NULL` guard, and one using `= NULL` instead of
+`IS NULL` all produce the correct branch count. All three were introduced as deliberate mutations
+and all three are caught by the triple assertions; none would have been caught by counting.
+
+
+Org-level grants can only be covered by unit tests. `POST /role-assignments` rejects them
+with `single-account-only` and there is no direct-insert path in e2e, so the `org` branch
+of `roleAssignmentMatchesScope` is exercised in `role-assignments.model.test.ts` only.
+
+Local e2e for this module needs a Basic-auth caller: the whole module is
+`requireServiceCaller()`, and assignment writes need a forwardable (Basic) credential.
+That means `LOCAL_BASIC_AUTH_*` populated, plus `E2E_REMOTE=true`, `E2E_BASIC_AUTH_TOKEN`
+(any value — a local Basic header is trusted and mapped to that identity), and
+`E2E_ACCOUNT_ID` matching `LOCAL_BASIC_AUTH_ACCOUNT_ID`. `E2E_REMOTE` is doing double duty
+here; in this suite it means "Basic caller", not "deployed host". Worth a dedicated flag
+separately.
+
+Implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-scoped-user-role-assignments.md`.

+-- Index for the scope-first read pattern introduced by
+-- GET /v1/scoped-user-role-assignments, which pages users by scope:
+--
+--   SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM user_role_assignments
+--   WHERE organization_id = ? AND environment = ?
+--     AND (<walk-up scope predicate on account_id/site_id/store_id>)
+--   ORDER BY user_id ASC LIMIT n + 1
+--
+-- Every existing read filters organization_id AND environment AND user_id, so
+-- leading with (organization_id, environment, user_id) serves them at least as
+-- well as idx_user_org did — which is why that index is REPLACED rather than
+-- supplemented. Keeping both costs write throughput for no read benefit.
+--
+-- Trailing account_id/site_id/store_id make the index cover every column the
+-- scoped query touches, so it can be answered by an index-only scan. They must
+-- be key columns, not INCLUDE: INCLUDE columns cannot be used as index
+-- qualifications, so an INCLUDE variant filters no rows and only inflates the
+-- index (measured 3x larger and slower than this shape).
+--
+-- Measured on 1.24M rows / 60 organizations:
+--   scoped query      30-72 ms  ->  0.02 ms (index-only scan, account/site
+--                                   query points) / 2.8 ms (store query point,
+--                                   where the planner switches to BitmapOr)
+--   existing reads    0.17 ms   ->  0.16 ms (unchanged)
+--   3000-row insert   257 ms    ->  206 ms  (faster: this index leads with
+--                                   low-cardinality organization_id, so a
+--                                   fan-out clusters into few pages, whereas
+--                                   idx_user_org led with random user_id)
+--
+-- CREATE INDEX is deliberately not CONCURRENTLY: migrate.ts runs each migration
+-- inside a transaction and CONCURRENTLY cannot run there. A plain build took
+-- 2.7 s for 1.24M rows and takes a SHARE lock, so reads continue and writes
+-- pause for the duration.
+
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ura_org_env_user_scope
+  ON user_role_assignments (
+    organization_id, environment, user_id, account_id, site_id, store_id
+  );
+
+DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_user_org;
